counterexample: For n=2, the set {u1,u2} consists of n distinct vertices of G but contains no original vertex, refuting step 0033. Also, when n=1, a one-vertex path may consist of an added isolated vertex, refuting later claims that PG cannot contain one.

0009: OK; continues the standard source-problem statement and reduction plan.

0011: OK; fixes an arbitrary source instance H with n vertices.
0012: OK; begins defining the target instance G.

0019: OK; states the equivalence that must be proved.
0020: OK; begins the forward implication.
0021: OK; assumes a Hamiltonian path visiting all n vertices of H.
0022: OK; the same vertex sequence can be considered in G.
0023: OK; every edge of H is retained in G.
0024: OK; this copied path visits all original vertices and no added vertices.
0025: OK; isolation also prevents traversal between U and the original graph.
0026: OK; PH remains a simple n-vertex path in G.
0027: OK; n=(n+17)-17=|VG|-17.
0028: OK; the forward implication follows.
0029: OK; begins the reverse implication.
0030: OK; assumes a target path PG with the required number of vertices.
0031: OK; its number of visited vertices is n.
0032: OK; simplicity makes those n vertices distinct.
0033: FAIL; an arbitrary n-element subset of the n+17 vertices need not contain all n original vertices.
0034: FAIL; “all original vertices (and possibly some added ones)” is also incompatible with the set having exactly n elements, although the proof next tries a different isolation argument.
0035: FAIL as stated for unrestricted n; when n=1, a one-vertex path can contain an isolated ui.
0036: OK; each ui has no incident edges.
0037: OK; a path containing an isolated vertex cannot contain another vertex.
0038: OK; any path containing an isolated vertex must be the singleton path at that vertex.
0039: FAIL; such a singleton does cover n vertices when n=1.
0040: FAIL; the proof assumes n>1 without having imposed or proved that restriction.
0041: FAIL; besides relying on n>1, H need not lie in one connected component, so “the connected component ... that contains H” is not generally defined.
0042: OK as a continuation of the observation that isolated vertices are separate components, but it does not repair the preceding issues.
0043: OK; page-number artifact with no mathematical content.
0044: OK; blank formatting artifact.
0045: FAIL for n=1; PG could be a singleton path at an added isolated vertex rather than a vertex of VH.
0046: FAIL; the assertion that this particular PG visits every vertex of H depends on the false step 0045.
0047: FAIL as an unconditional inference; it is correct only if PG has first been shown to use all of VH.
0048: OK conditionally; edges of G between original vertices are exactly EH.
0049: FAIL as proved; the n=1 case would make the conclusion true, but it requires a separate argument not supplied here.
0050: FAIL as a claimed completed derivation; the equivalence is in fact salvageable, but the written reverse proof has not handled n=1 and contains false assertions.
0051: OK; the construction itself is polynomial-time.
0052: FAIL in calling the reduction established, because the preceding equivalence proof is incomplete as written.
0053: FAIL as an inference within this proof; NP-hardness would follow after repairing the reverse direction, for example by separately treating n=1 or restricting the source instances to n>1.
0054: OK regarding membership in NP, but the NP-completeness/completion claim inherits the unresolved proof defect.
0055: OK; page-number artifact with no mathematical content.
